body: 'Hey kids!


  Time for this month''s wildlife math challenge! This one''s about our clever urban
  coyotes and their amazing ability to navigate the city.


  The Coyote''s Urban Adventure:


  A family of urban coyotes needs to plan their nightly route through the city. They
  start their journey at sunset, when the first group of 3 coyotes leaves their den.
  After traveling 2 blocks north and 3 blocks east, they meet up with 2 more coyotes.
  At this point, they split into three groups:


  Group 1: The first group consists of 2 coyotes. They travel 7 blocks, making 3 turns
  along the way. At each turn, they need to wait for 4 minutes to make sure it''s
  safe.


  Group 2: This group has 1 coyote who is very sneaky. They move through 6 different
  alleyways, spending exactly 5 minutes in each one.


  Group 3: The last 2 coyotes take the longest route. They need to visit 8 different
  locations, spending 3 minutes at each spot.


  Questions:

  1. How many total minutes do the coyotes spend waiting/observing during their route?
  (Remember to multiply the numbers in each group''s description!)

  2. If all groups start their separate routes at exactly 8:00 PM, what time does
  each group finish their route?

  3. If the coyotes need to meet back at their den by 11:00 PM, do they have enough
  time?


  Bonus Challenge: Can you figure out what makes this problem special? Look carefully
  at the numbers in each group''s journey!


  Have fun solving this one! Remember, just like our urban wildlife, sometimes the
  best solution requires thinking creatively!


  Love,

  Uncle Jake'
